formation.title: The Unification of Nusantara
formation.text:
The dream of Gajah Mada is realized anew. From the rice paddies of Java to the spice groves of the Moluccas, from the trading ports of Sumatra to the shores of Sulawesi, the scattered islands of the archipelago answer to a single authority. The concept of Nusantara, the entirety of the island realm between the seas, is no longer a poet's vision but a political reality.

But what kind of realm shall this be? The archipelago's power can be projected outward through fleets that command every strait and sea lane, binding vassals through maritime supremacy as Srivijaya once did. Or it can be turned inward, cultivating the extraordinary wealth that flows from controlling the source of the world's most precious spices, making Nusantara not a conqueror of seas, but an indispensable marketplace that the whole world must court.

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: Our fleets shall command every strait

modifiers.name: Mandala Thalassocracy
modifiers.text: Nusantara rules as a maritime mandala, concentric rings of sovereignty extending outward from sacred Java across ten thousand islands, each vassal bound by trade and tribute to the center.

options.text: The world will come to us for spice

modifiers.name: Spice Archipelago
modifiers.text: The cloves of Ternate, the nutmeg of Banda, the pepper of Banten, Nusantara controls the sources of the world's most coveted goods, and every merchant vessel that passes through these waters enriches the archipelago.

advances.name: Srivijaya Maritime Legacy
advances.text: The traditions of Srivijaya, the archipelago's first great thalassocratic empire, live on in the seamanship and maritime commerce of Nusantara.

advances.name: Sawah Irrigation
advances.text: The subak water temple system manages the intricate terraced rice paddies that feed the dense populations of Java and Bali.

advances.name: Ancient Spice Knowledge
advances.text: Generations of cultivation and trade in cloves, nutmeg, and pepper give Nusantara unmatched expertise in the world's most valuable commodities.

advances.name: Silat Martial Tradition
advances.text: Pencak silat, the indigenous martial art of the archipelago, trains warriors in fluid close-combat techniques developed through centuries of inter-island warfare.

advances.name: Mandala Statecraft
advances.text: The mandala model of governance binds vassals through concentric rings of influence radiating from a sacred center, allowing the archipelago to be governed without rigid borders.

advances.name: Majapahit Golden Age
advances.text: Under Hayam Wuruk and Gajah Mada, Majapahit united the archipelago from its capital at Trowulan, creating the model for Nusantara's political unity.

event.title: The Majapahit Golden Age
event.text:
In the year 1365, the court poet Prapanca composed the Nagarakretagama, describing a realm that stretched from Sumatra to Papua, from Borneo to Bali. At its center sat King Hayam Wuruk in the capital of Trowulan, a city of canals and temples, of red brick candi rising above the rice plains of eastern Java.

But the true architect of this empire was the Mahapatih Gajah Mada, who swore the legendary Palapa Oath: he would not taste spice until the entire archipelago was united under Majapahit's banner. Through a combination of military campaigns, diplomatic marriages, and trade alliances, he made good on his word. The question now is whether to follow his path of conquest outward, or to perfect the civilization he built at home.

options.text: We honor Gajah Mada's oath; the archipelago is ours by right

modifiers.name: Oath of Gajah Mada
modifiers.text: As Gajah Mada once swore to unite all Nusantara under a single banner, so too does the realm now pursue the completion of his vision through military strength and righteous conquest.

options.text: Trowulan shall outshine every capital in the world

modifiers.name: Splendor of Trowulan
modifiers.text: The capital blazes with the red brick grandeur of a hundred candi temples. Poets, architects, and scholars gather at a court that rivals any in the known world.

advances.name: Kris Warrior Tradition
advances.text: The kris, the asymmetrical wavy-bladed dagger of Java, is both sacred heirloom and weapon of war, wielded by elite warriors trained in the art of silat.

advances.name: Candi Temple Tradition
advances.text: The red brick candi temples of eastern Java represent centuries of Hindu-Buddhist architectural mastery, centers of learning and devotion.

advances.name: Pasar Trading Tradition
advances.text: The great pasar marketplaces of Nusantara are where the products of a thousand islands converge, spices from the east, textiles from the west, rice from Java's heartland.

advances.name: Archipelagic Navigation
advances.text: Navigating ten thousand islands requires mastery of currents, monsoon winds, and star paths passed down through generations of seafaring peoples.

advances.name: Prahu Raider Fleet
advances.text: The double-outrigger prahu is the fastest vessel in island waters, ideal for raiding, coastal patrol, and the pursuit of enemy shipping through narrow straits.

advances.name: Islamic Scholarship
advances.text: Islam spread peacefully through the archipelago via Sufi traders and scholars. The pesantren boarding schools became centers of both religious learning and Javanese intellectual life.

advances.name: Spice Monopoly
advances.text: Control of the Moluccan spice sources, the world's only supply of cloves and nutmeg, gives Nusantara unparalleled leverage in global trade.

event.title: Masters of the Spice Trade
event.text:
For centuries, the tiny volcanic islands of the Moluccas produced the only cloves and nutmeg in the world. The Banda Islands, barely visible specks in the vast ocean, supplied every grain of mace and nutmeg consumed from China to Venice. And it was the merchants and sultans of Nusantara who controlled the first and most profitable links in this chain, buying from growers, storing in great gudang warehouses, and selling to Arab, Indian, and Chinese traders at enormous markup.

Now this monopoly has been consolidated under a single political authority. Where once a dozen competing sultanates undercut each other, Nusantara speaks with one voice and sets one price. The world has no choice but to pay it.

options.text: The spice must flow, through our hands alone

advances.name: Cetbang Bronze Foundries
advances.text: The Javanese cetbang cannon, cast in bronze, demonstrates an indigenous gunpowder tradition that predates European contact in the archipelago.

advances.name: Shipbuilding Mastery
advances.text: The galangan kapal royal shipyards produce jong, prahu, and kora-kora in quantities that make Nusantara a naval power to be reckoned with.

advances.name: Sultanate Governance
advances.text: The Islamic sultanates formalize archipelagic governance through syariah courts, harbor masters, and a bureaucracy adapted to the realities of island rule.

advances.name: Kora-Kora War Fleet
advances.text: The kora-kora is a massive Moluccan war galley crewed by hundreds of warriors, designed for the boarding actions and close-quarters naval combat of island warfare.

advances.name: Pepper and Spice Exports
advances.text: Banten, Aceh, and a dozen other ports funnel the archipelago's pepper, cloves, and nutmeg into the arteries of global commerce.

advances.name: Wayang Court Arts
advances.text: The shadow puppet theater of wayang kulit transmits the epic stories of the Ramayana and Mahabharata, binding diverse peoples through shared cultural heritage.

advances.name: Fortress of Resistance
advances.text: Coastal and inland benteng fortifications arise to defend Nusantara against European colonial incursions and assert sovereignty over the archipelago.

advances.name: Sultan Agung's Campaigns
advances.text: Sultan Agung of Mataram's sieges of Batavia in 1628-1629 demonstrated both the military potential and the fierce determination of Javanese resistance to colonialism.

event.title: Sultan Agung's Siege of Batavia
event.text:
In 1628, Sultan Agung of Mataram assembled the largest Javanese army in living memory and marched on Batavia, the fortified trading post of the VOC that had planted itself uninvited on the north coast of Java. His forces numbered in the tens of thousands, supported by war elephants and bronze cetbang cannon. The siege was a titanic clash between Javanese sovereignty and European commercial imperialism.

Though the first siege failed due to supply difficulties and Dutch naval superiority, Agung launched a second attempt in 1629, this time attempting to establish rice granaries along the route. The campaigns revealed both the military potential and the logistical challenges of resisting a naval power from a land base. Agung's legacy endures: he proved that Nusantara would not submit without a fight.

options.text: We shall learn from Agung's campaigns and strike harder

modifiers.name: Agung's Military Reform
modifiers.text: Sultan Agung's campaigns against Batavia demonstrated that the defense of Nusantara demands offensive capability: the ability to project force, sustain sieges, and drive foreign interlopers from the archipelago.

options.text: Agung was wise to fortify. Let no invader hold our soil

modifiers.name: Agung's Consolidation
modifiers.text: The lesson of Batavia is not that the siege failed, but that no foreign fortress should have been permitted to rise in the first place. Every coast must be watched, every approach defended, every invader bled by attrition.

advances.name: Phinisi Sailing Tradition
advances.text: The phinisi, a two-masted sailing vessel of Bugis-Makassar design, represents the pinnacle of Indonesian shipbuilding, fast, seaworthy, and built for long voyages.

advances.name: Bugis Diaspora
advances.text: The Bugis and Makassar peoples of Sulawesi are the archipelago's greatest seafarers, traders, mercenaries, and colonists who establish communities from Borneo to the Malay Peninsula.

advances.name: Mataram Statecraft
advances.text: The Sultanate of Mataram centralizes Javanese political authority, combining Islamic governance with pre-existing Javanese administrative traditions.

advances.name: Anti-Colonial Resistance
advances.text: From Aceh to Ternate, from Banten to Mataram, the peoples of Nusantara organize sustained resistance against European colonial encroachment.

advances.name: Nusantara Awakening
advances.text: A new consciousness emerges: the archipelago is not merely a collection of kingdoms but a single civilization united by shared seas and intertwined destinies.

event.title: The Nusantara Awakening
event.text:
From Aceh to Papua, from the mountains of Sumatra to the spice groves of Ternate, a new idea takes hold: that the archipelago is not merely a collection of kingdoms and sultanates, but a single civilization bound by shared seas, interwoven trade, and centuries of cultural exchange. Javanese, Sundanese, Malay, Bugis, Balinese, Moluccan: the peoples of the islands are many, but the ocean that connects them is one.

This is the awakening of Nusantara consciousness, the realization that unity does not require uniformity, that a thousand islands can share a single destiny without abandoning their distinct identities. Gotong royong, the ancient tradition of communal labor and mutual aid, becomes the philosophical foundation of a modern state.

options.text: Bhinneka Tunggal Ika, unity in diversity

advances.name: Spice Industrialization
advances.text: Modern processing, packaging, and export methods transform the archipelago's ancient spice trade into an industrial enterprise of global scale.

advances.name: Maritime Sovereignty
advances.text: Nusantara asserts sovereign control over the waters between its islands, the sea is not a border but the connective tissue of the nation.

advances.name: Gotong Royong
advances.text: The ancient Indonesian tradition of communal mutual aid becomes a governing philosophy, the state thrives when all its peoples labor together for the common good.

advances.name: Pancasila Foundations
advances.text: Unity in diversity, the philosophical principle that a nation of hundreds of cultures, languages, and faiths can coexist under a shared commitment to tolerance and mutual respect.

destiny.name: The Nusantara Mandate
destiny.text: With the archipelago unified under a single banner, the mandate of heaven falls upon Nusantara. Stability must be maintained as the foundation for greater ambitions.

event.title: The Nusantara Mandate
event.text:
The scattered kingdoms and sultanates of the archipelago have been gathered under one crown. From the volcanic peaks of Java to the coral atolls of the eastern seas, Nusantara stands as a unified realm for the first time since the golden age of Majapahit.

But unity alone is not destiny. The mandate to rule ten thousand islands demands more than military conquest, it demands stability, legitimacy, and a vision for what this unprecedented archipelagic state can become. The foundations have been laid. Now the real work begins.

options.text: The mandate of the archipelago is ours

destiny.name: Masters of the Strait
destiny.text: Seize control of the Strait of Malacca, the narrow passage through which all trade between the Indian Ocean and the South China Sea must flow. The Malay Peninsula must bend to Nusantara's will.

conditions.text: Own Malacca, or a subject owns it
Own Kedah, or a subject owns it

event.title: Masters of the Strait
event.text:
The flags of Nusantara now fly over Malacca and Kedah, the chokepoints of the world's busiest maritime trade route. Every Chinese junk carrying silk to the west, every Arab dhow laden with frankincense, every Indian vessel bearing textiles and gemstones, all must pass through waters that Nusantara commands.

Srivijaya understood this power seven centuries ago. The Malacca Sultanate built an empire upon it. Now Nusantara inherits their legacy and surpasses it, for no previous maritime power controlled both sides of the strait simultaneously while also commanding the vast archipelago to the south and east.

options.text: All who sail these waters sail by our leave

destiny.name: Dominion Over the Champa Seas
destiny.text: With Malacca secured, project Nusantara's maritime power northward into the waters of Champa and the Gulf of Siam. Establish naval supremacy over the entire South China Sea.

conditions.text: Own Vijaya, or a subject owns it
Own Pattani, or a subject owns it

event.title: The South China Sea Campaign
event.text:
Nusantara's war fleets now patrol waters that stretch from the Mekong Delta to the Gulf of Siam. The old kingdom of Champa, the Malay coastal cities, and the trading ports of the mainland all acknowledge the supremacy of the archipelago's navy.

The question is how to consolidate this far-flung maritime dominion. Some admirals advocate for aggressive forward deployment, maintaining battle fleets in distant waters, ready to project power at a moment's notice. Others counsel a subtler approach, using the strait chokepoints as leverage for diplomatic hegemony, binding mainland states through trade dependence rather than occupation.

options.text: Our war fleets will patrol every sea lane

modifiers.name: Fleet Projection Doctrine
modifiers.text: Nusantara's war fleets maintain permanent stations in distant waters, ready to project power at a moment's notice. War is cheap and decisive for those who control the sea.

options.text: Let the straits do our work for us

modifiers.name: Strait Hegemony
modifiers.text: Rather than patrolling every sea lane by force, Nusantara uses its chokepoint control as diplomatic leverage, binding mainland states through intelligence networks and trade dependence.

destiny.name: Samudra Raja
destiny.text: Lord of the Seas. Plant Nusantara's banner on the mainland itself, from the Mekong Delta to the Chao Phraya, the maritime empire extends its reach beyond the archipelago. Build the Benteng Laut coastal command to anchor this dominion.

conditions.text: Own Ayodhya, or a subject owns it

event.title: Samudra Raja: Lord of the Seas
event.text:
From the rice plains of the Chao Phraya to the spice groves of the Moluccas, from the Strait of Malacca to the Timor Sea, Nusantara's writ runs over the greatest maritime domain the world has ever seen. No naval power, not the Portuguese, not the Dutch, not the Chinese treasure fleets, can challenge our supremacy in these waters.

The Samudra Raja, the Lord of the Seas, faces a final choice. The empire can be secured through overwhelming naval and military force, modernizing the armed forces to crush any challenger. Or it can be anchored in permanent institutions, garrisons at every strait, fortresses at every harbor, a network of naval bases that will outlast any individual ruler.

modifiers.name: Naval Supremacy Doctrine
modifiers.text: The modernization of Nusantara's military ensures tactical superiority over any rival, though the cost of maintaining such forces strains the treasury.

options.text: Build the permanent institutions of empire

modifiers.name: Institutions of the Samudra
modifiers.text: A permanent network of garrisons and naval bases anchors Nusantara's maritime empire, though the costs of empire drive up the price of borrowing.

destiny.name: Command the Spice Sources
destiny.text: The clove trees of Ternate and the nutmeg groves of Banda produce the world's most valuable commodities. Bring these distant Moluccan sultanates firmly under Nusantara's control.

conditions.text: Own Ternate, or a subject owns it
Own Banda, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Spice Islands Under One Crown
event.text:
Ternate and Banda, for centuries, these tiny volcanic islands in the eastern seas were the only source of cloves and nutmeg on earth. Local sultans grew fabulously wealthy, playing Portuguese, Spanish, and Dutch traders against each other while the price of a single sack of cloves could buy a ship in Venice.

Now these legendary spice islands answer to Nusantara. The middlemen have been eliminated. The growers, the warehouses, the ships, and the ports are all under a single authority. For the first time, the entire spice supply chain, from tree to ship, is controlled by one power.

options.text: The spice flows through our hands alone

destiny.name: The Greatest Emporium
destiny.text: Transform Nusantara from a spice producer into the world's greatest trading emporium. Build Gresik, the port of the eastern spice fleets, up into a great harbor city, and raise a Pelabuhan Niaga, a trading port in the Srivijaya tradition, on its waterfront.

conditions.text: Gresik is held and its development is at least 38
We hold Gresik and a Pelabuhan Niaga stands there

event.title: The Emporium of the East
event.text:
The ports of Nusantara have become the crossroads of the world. Chinese merchants bring porcelain and silk, Indian traders carry textiles and gemstones, Arab voyagers offer frankincense and horses, and European ships arrive laden with silver. All come to buy what only these islands produce, and all leave paying Nusantara's price.

Two philosophies compete at court. The monopolists argue for a tight cartel, control supply, fix prices, punish smugglers, and extract maximum profit from every grain of spice. The free traders counter that an open emporium attracts more merchants, more goods, more ideas, and ultimately more wealth than any monopoly could squeeze from a restricted market.

options.text: Control supply and fix the price

modifiers.name: Spice Cartel
modifiers.text: Nusantara enforces a tight monopoly on the global spice trade, controlling supply, fixing prices, and extending its commercial reach to distant markets.

options.text: Welcome all merchants to our open ports

modifiers.name: Open Emporium
modifiers.text: The ports of Nusantara welcome merchants from every nation, attracting a cosmopolitan population of traders, settlers, and mercenaries, though the military grows soft in this atmosphere of commerce.

destiny.name: Bumi Rempah
destiny.text: The Land of Spices. Every merchant vessel on earth, from Lisbon to Canton, depends on the commodities that grow only in these islands. Hold Gowa, the harbor of Makassar where the spice ships gather, and build it up. Then raise the Pasar Dunia, the World Market, and let all nations come to Nusantara with gold in hand.

conditions.text: Gowa is held and its development is at least 40

children.text: Cloves is produced in the market
Cloves is traded in the market

event.title: Bumi Rempah: The Land of Spices
event.text:
Nusantara is not merely a country that trades in spices: it IS spice. The economy of the entire known world depends on commodities that grow only in these islands. No European colonial venture, no Chinese tribute mission, no Arab trading fleet can function without what Nusantara produces. The Land of Spices has become the indispensable nation.

This supreme economic position can be leveraged in different ways. Some counsel building the world's greatest marketplace, a permanent institution where all nations must come to trade, enriching the archipelago through the sheer volume of commerce. Others advocate for cultural and political hegemony, using economic leverage to project Nusantara's civilization outward, integrating diverse peoples into an ever-expanding sphere of influence.

modifiers.name: World Marketplace
modifiers.text: The Pasar Dunia is an institution without parallel, a permanent marketplace where all nations come to trade. The archipelago feeds itself with ease, though maintaining the fortifications to protect this wealth is costly.

options.text: Our wealth shall project our civilization

modifiers.name: Spice Empire
modifiers.text: Economic supremacy becomes cultural hegemony. Nusantara's wealth funds an expansion of civilizational influence, integrating diverse peoples and projecting the archipelago's culture across the region.

units.name: Kris Warriors
units.text: Elite Javanese infantry wielding the sacred kris dagger, trained in the ancient martial art of pencak silat. Their fighting style emphasizes sudden, devastating close-quarters strikes.

units.name: Kris Levy Warriors
units.text: Levy troops armed with the traditional kris, drawn from the villages and rice paddies of Java.

units.name: Cetbang Artillery
units.text: Bronze cannons cast in the Javanese tradition, predating European gunpowder weapons in the archipelago. The cetbang fires stone or iron projectiles with deadly accuracy.

units.name: Prahu Raider
units.text: A swift double-outrigger vessel built for speed and maneuverability in the shallow waters and narrow straits of the archipelago. Ideal for coastal raiding and pursuit.

units.name: Kora-Kora War Galley
units.text: A massive Moluccan war galley designed for boarding actions and close-quarters naval combat, crewed by hundreds of warriors from the spice islands.

units.name: Kora-Kora Levy Galley
units.text: War galleys crewed by levied islanders from the coastal communities of Nusantara.

units.name: Phinisi
units.text: The celebrated two-masted sailing vessel of Bugis-Makassar design, built for long ocean voyages. Fast and seaworthy, the phinisi dominates late-era Indonesian maritime trade and warfare.

buildings.name: Candi Temple
buildings.text: A red brick Hindu-Buddhist temple complex in the east Javanese tradition, serving as a center of religious devotion, cultural learning, and artistic patronage.

buildings.name: Pasar Agung
buildings.text: The Great Marketplace, a central bazaar where the products of ten thousand islands converge. Spices, textiles, precious metals, and ceramics flow through its stalls.

buildings.name: Galangan Kapal
buildings.text: A royal shipyard in the Javanese and Bugis tradition, producing jong, prahu, kora-kora, and phinisi for Nusantara's merchant and war fleets.

buildings.name: Benteng Perlawanan
buildings.text: A fortress of resistance, coastal and inland fortifications built to repel colonial invaders and assert Nusantara's sovereignty over its territory.

buildings.name: Pesantren
buildings.text: An Islamic boarding school in the Javanese tradition, where students study the Quran alongside Javanese literature, mathematics, and natural philosophy.

buildings.name: Sawah Terasering
buildings.text: Irrigated rice terraces managed by the subak water temple system, a marvel of agricultural engineering that sustains Java's dense population. Each new tier of terraces makes the land yield more rice.

where.text: The location's raw material is Rice

buildings.name: Padepokan Silat
buildings.text: A training ground for the ancient martial art of pencak silat, where warriors master the fluid combat techniques of the archipelago.

buildings.name: Gudang Rempah
buildings.text: A spice warehouse where cloves, nutmeg, pepper, and other precious trade goods are stored, graded, and prepared for export to the world's markets.

buildings.name: Pendopo Wayang
buildings.text: An open-air performance hall where the dalang puppeteer performs wayang kulit, shadow puppet theater that transmits the great epics and unifies the cultures of the archipelago.

buildings.name: Pelabuhan Niaga
buildings.text: A great trading port in the Srivijaya tradition, serving as an entrepot where goods from across the Indian Ocean and the South China Sea change hands.

buildings.name: Benteng Laut
buildings.text: A coastal naval command fortress, combining harbor defense, fleet anchorage, and garrison quarters to project Nusantara's maritime power over distant seas and straits.

buildings.name: Pasar Dunia
buildings.text: The World Market, a vast permanent trading complex where merchants from every nation converge to buy and sell the world's most coveted goods. The ultimate expression of Nusantara's economic supremacy.

list.name: Pamget Tributary Apparatus
list.text: The Negarakertagama palm-leaf register of 1365, composed by the court poet Mpu Prapanca for King Hayam Wuruk, lists the mancanagara outer countries and the nusantara islands proper as a graded mandala of tributaries. Each year envoys carried pamget deliveries of gold, slaves, cloves, and aromatic woods to Trowulan; in return the outer rulers were inscribed in royal registers and confirmed in their thrones. The system extended Majapahit's sphere from the Malay peninsula through Sulawesi to western New Guinea, but its lightness of touch (annual tribute, not garrisons) meant that royal weakness anywhere on the chain invited rebellion across it.

list.name: Sumpah Palapa Court Ritual
list.text: Patih Gajah Mada, taking office in 1336, swore before the boy-king Hayam Wuruk that he would taste no spice, no palapa, until the archipelago was unified under Majapahit. The oath was institutionalized in the annual Caitra festival at Trowulan, where each Bhre prince and tributary raja, in ranked court robes, renewed allegiance while the patih recited the territorial litany of nusantara. Fusing Hindu-Buddhist royal ceremony with a secular doctrine of pan-archipelagic sovereignty, the ritual subordinated the great regional kings to a single ritual axis: the foundation stone of every later Nusantara rhetoric.

children.text: Has primary or accepted culture is Javanese
Has primary or accepted culture is Sundanese

list.name: Pasisir Coastal Confederation
list.text: The chain of north-Java port sultanates (Demak founded c.1475, then Cirebon, Banten, Tuban, and Gresik) whose syahbandar harbour-masters and bandar magistrates governed cosmopolitan populations of Javanese, Malay, Hokkien, Gujarati, Arab, and Bugis traders. After Demak's overthrow of Majapahit around 1527 the pasisir held the political weight of Java. A loose council of sultans coordinated convoy escorts, tariff rates, and the Friday markets that drew the Moluccan spice trade to Java's coasts, power resting with merchant-sultans and ulama-trader notables against the older inland aristocracy.

list.name: Wali Songo Missionary Network
list.text: The Nine Saints of Java (Sunan Kalijaga, Sunan Bonang, Sunan Giri, and their fellows) wove Islam into Javanese culture from c.1450 to c.1550 through wayang puppet theatre, gamelan music, and the gradual conversion of the courts of Demak, Cirebon, and Mataram. They founded pesantren religious schools, composed Suluk mystical poetry, and built tomb-shrines that still draw pilgrims. The kyai spiritual lineages they founded became the religious backbone of Javanese Islam, but their populist piety unsettled the Hindu-Buddhist priyayi aristocracy whose courts had defined Javanese high culture for a thousand years.

list.name: Tumenggung Regency System
list.text: Sultan Agung of Mataram, reigning 1613 to 1645, replaced the old Bhre cadet-princedoms of the Javanese hinterland with tumenggung regents: crown-appointed officials drawn from royal kinsmen and trusted santri commanders, charged with provincial revenue, road corvée, and the levy of prajurit infantry for Mataram's wars. The system pulled administrative weight inland from the pasisir coast, imposed a uniform Javanese court culture across the heartland, and made Mataram briefly the strongest land power in the archipelago, but it also sidelined the merchant-sultans whose wealth had funded the Islamic conversion of Java.

list.name: Kapitan Ethnic Magistracy
list.text: In Malacca, Banten, Aceh, Makassar, and the Mataram pasisir, the sultan appointed a kapitan (captain, from Portuguese capitão) to govern each foreign or non-Muslim community under its own customary law. The Kapitan Cina led the Hokkien and Cantonese quarters; the Kapitan Kling spoke for Tamil and Gujarati traders; the Kapitan Bugis led migrant settlers at non-Malay courts. The kapitan registered births, settled disputes, collected the head-tax, and answered for his community to the syahbandar: a peculiarly archipelagic institution that freed the sultan from governing diasporas directly while binding their wealth to the throne.
